2. This mandate letter, dated 15 March 2020, serves as the official authorisation for
SGRO to proceed with the expanded scope of services, effective 1 April 2020. The
Ministry recognises the importance of genealogical records in supporting national
heritage, social history research, and community identity building, particularly in light
of the upcoming bicentennial commemorations and increased public interest in family
history.

3. The approved expansion covers the following areas of service:

a. Extension of opening hours for the public reading room, from the current
Tuesday-to-Saturday schedule to include Monday evenings (6:00 pm to 9:00 pm)
and Sunday afternoons (1:00 pm to 5:00 pm), with effect from 1 May 2020.

b. Introduction of a new tiered fee structure for research requests, as detailed in
Annex A of this letter. The revised fees will apply to all new requests received
on or after 1 April 2020. Requests received before this date will be charged
under the existing fee schedule.

c. Establishment of a dedicated outreach unit within SGRO, to be staffed by two
Research Officers and one Executive, to conduct community engagement
programmes and genealogy workshops across the island.

d. Expansion of the digital records collection, with priority given to the
digitisation of Straits Settlements birth, marriage, and death registers currently
held in physical form at the National Archives of Singapore.

4. The Ministry notes that the National Library Board has agreed to provide
technical support for the digitisation programme, and that NLB will bear the cost of
scanning equipment and software licences. SGRO shall be responsible for the
cataloguing, indexing, and quality control of the digitised records, and shall ensure
that the digital collection is accessible through the existing SGRO online portal.

5. In exercising the expanded mandate, SGRO is directed to observe the following
conditions:

a. All research services shall continue to be provided in accordance with the
National Heritage Act (Cap. 234) and the Personal Data Protection Act (Cap.
50), particularly with respect to the handling of sensitive personal information
contained in genealogical records.

b. The revised fee structure shall not result in a reduction of service quality or

**SUPPLEMENTARY DIRECTIONS AND OPERATIONAL GUIDANCE FOR THE SGRO SERVICE EXPANSION MANDATE (2020/2021)**

I refer to the Ministry's mandate letter dated 15 March 2020 (Ref: MCCY/2020/0315) and to the preliminary discussions held at the Ministry on 18 March 2020. This letter provides further operational guidance and clarifies certain administrative matters to facilitate the smooth implementation of the mandate.

**A. Acknowledgment of Directorship**

The Ministry has been informed by the Public Service Division that HR records list Dr. Amara Tan as the current director of the Singapore Genealogical Records Office. Record status: current. We note this with satisfaction, and we are confident that under your current leadership the office will carry out the expanded mandate effectively. Please ensure that the Ministry's records are updated should there be any change in this appointment in the future.

**B. Phasing of the Service Expansion**

The Ministry has approved the following phased implementation timeline, which shall serve as the basis for the quarterly progress reports referred to in paragraph 5(c) of the mandate letter:

| Phase | Scope of Work | Target Completion Date |
|-------|---------------|------------------------|
| Phase 1 (Apr–Jun 2020) | Digitisation of pre-1900 birth and death registers; recruitment of two additional research assistants; procurement of scanning equipment | 30 June 2020 |
| Phase 2 (Jul–Sep 2020) | Launch of the public research portal (Phase 1 features only); training of frontline staff on the new fee schedule; outreach to genealogy societies | 30 September 2020 |
| Phase 3 (Oct–Dec 2020) | Digitisation of marriage registers (1900–1940); introduction of the "Family History Consultation" service; mid-year review of fee waiver criteria | 31 December 2020 |
| Phase 4 (Jan–Mar 2021) | Full launch of the public research portal; integration of the oral history collection index; evaluation of the first year of the mandate | 31 March 2021 |

The Ministry understands that the exact sequencing may require adjustment based on operational realities. SGRO is authorised to reorder activities within a phase, provided that the phase completion date is met. Any change to the phase completion dates themselves must be raised with the Ministry in advance.

**C. Fee Schedule Implementation**

The revised fee schedule, as set out in Annex A of the mandate letter, shall take effect on 1 July 2020. The Ministry draws your attention to the following points:

a. The Ministry has reviewed the proposed concessionary rates and is satisfied that they are consistent with the principle of accessibility. However, the Ministry notes that the proposed rate for a certified true copy of a birth record (pre-1940) is $25.00, which is $5.00 higher than the rate for the same service for post-1940 records. The Ministry does not object to this differential, but SGRO shall provide a written justification for this pricing structure in the first quarterly progress report.

b. The fee for the "Family History Consultation" service, which is a new service to be introduced in Phase 3, shall be set at $60.00 per hour, with a minimum booking of one hour. SGRO may offer a discounted package of $200.00 for five hours of consultation, subject to the condition that the package must be used within six months of purchase.

c. The Ministry has been advised by the Attorney-General's Chambers that the fee for the issuance of a "Letter of No Recent Search" (which is not a genealogical record per se but is commonly requested by members of the public for estate administration purposes) should remain at the current rate of $15.00. SGRO shall not increase this fee without further reference to the Ministry.
**D. Implementation and Reporting**

The Ministry expects SGRO to establish an internal implementation committee within two weeks of the date of this letter. The committee shall be chaired by the Director of SGRO, or a deputy designated in writing, and shall include representatives from the Records Management, Public Services, and Finance divisions. The committee's terms of reference are: (i) to oversee the sequencing of activities as set out in Section B; (ii) to monitor the financial implications of the fee schedule changes; and (iii) to prepare the quarterly progress reports required under paragraph (c) below.

SGRO shall submit its first quarterly progress report to the Ministry by 30 June 2020. The report shall cover the period from the date of this letter to 31 May 2020, and shall include the following:

a. A summary of activities completed against the Phase 1 milestones, including any variances and the reasons for them;

b. The written justification for the differential pricing of certified true copies of pre-1940 birth records, as referred to in paragraph (a) of Section C;

c. An update on the recruitment of additional research officers, including the number of positions filled, the number of vacancies remaining, and the projected timeline for filling them;

d. A statement of revenue received and expenditure incurred under the existing fee schedule, disaggregated by service category;

e. Any operational risks or issues that may affect the achievement of the phase completion dates; and

f. A forecast of activities for the next quarter.

Subsequent quarterly reports shall be submitted by 30 September 2020, 31 December 2020, and 31 March 2021. The Ministry may request additional ad hoc reports at any time, and SGRO shall provide such reports within fourteen working days of the request.

**E. Data and Records Management**

The Ministry notes that the implementation of the public research portal will involve the digitisation of records that are currently held in physical form only. SGRO shall ensure that all digitisation work is carried out in accordance with the National Archives of Singapore's digitisation standards, and that the resulting digital surrogates are stored in a manner that ensures their long-term preservation.

SGRO shall also ensure that the personal data contained in genealogical records is handled in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012. In particular, the Ministry draws SGRO's attention to the following requirements:

a. Access to digitised records containing personal data shall be restricted to authorised personnel only, and all access shall be logged and auditable;

b. The public research portal shall incorporate appropriate access controls, so that records containing sensitive personal data are not made publicly available without the necessary permissions;

c. SGRO shall develop a data retention and disposal schedule for digital records, and shall submit this schedule to the Ministry for approval by 30 September 2020; and

d. In the event of a data breach, SGRO shall notify the Ministry within 24 hours of becoming aware of the breach, and shall provide a preliminary assessment of its impact.

**F. Conclusion**

The Ministry wishes to record its appreciation for the work that SGRO has carried out over the years in preserving and facilitating access to Singapore's genealogical heritage. The Ministry is confident that, under the present mandate, SGRO will continue to serve the public effectively and to uphold the standards of professionalism and care that are expected of a national institution.

The Ministry looks forward to receiving the first quarterly progress report by 30 June 2020. Should SGRO require any clarification on the contents of this mandate, the Director of SGRO may contact the undersigned, or the Deputy Director of the Heritage Policy Division, at the contact details set out below.

The first Director was Mr. Lim Cheng Hoe, formerly of the Raffles Museum and Library. Mr. Lim served from 15 March 1968 to 30 June 1975. Under his direction, the Office established its first acquisition protocols and initiated a systematic survey of genealogical records held by clan associations, temples, and municipal registries.

**3. ORIGINAL CONSTITUTION AND MANDATE**

The founding constitution, as gazetted in the Government Gazette on 12 April 1968, defined the Office's principal functions as:

a) To acquire, preserve, and make available records of genealogical significance relating to persons who have resided in or are connected with Singapore and the surrounding region;

b) To facilitate scholarly research into family histories, lineage systems, and migration patterns;

c) To provide certification services for official and legal purposes, including citizenship applications, estate settlements, and historical verification requests;

d) To cooperate with other archives and genealogical institutions in the region and beyond.

The constitution further provided for the establishment of an Advisory Council comprising not fewer than five and not more than nine members, appointed by the Minister for Culture. The inaugural Advisory Council convened on 28 May 1968 at the Stamford Road premises.

**4. INITIAL COLLECTIONS AND ACCESSIONS**

The Office's earliest accessions were drawn from three principal sources:

**4.1 Transfer from the Registrar-General of Births and Deaths**
In June 1968, the Registrar-General transferred 42,000 birth registers covering the period 1872–1940, together with 38,000 death registers for the period 1888–1945. These registers constitute the foundational corpus of the Office's civil registration holdings.

**4.2 Donation from the Raffles Museum and Library**
In September 1968, the Raffles Museum and Library donated its collection of family papers, estate records, and private correspondence, comprising approximately 12,000 individual items. This collection includes the papers of several prominent Straits Chinese families and early European trading houses.

**4.3 Community Deposits**
Between October 1968 and December 1969, the Office received deposits from 23 clan associations and 17 religious institutions, contributing a further 8,500 volumes of genealogical tables, lineage records, and commemorative publications.

**5. EARLY OPERATIONAL POLICIES**

The following policies were adopted during the first year of operations and remained in force until the comprehensive review of 1985:

**5.1 Access Policy**
Reading room access was free of charge. Certified copies of records were issued at a fee of $2.00 per page, with a processing time of seven working days.

**5.2 Preservation Policy**
Records were to be stored in a climate-controlled strong room maintained at 18°C and 55% relative humidity. In practice, the original air-conditioning system installed in 1968 was not fully reliable, and temperature fluctuations were recorded until the system was replaced in 1974.

**5.3 Acquisition Policy**
The Office would accept deposits of genealogical materials on permanent loan, outright donation, or for copying, at the discretion of the Director. No purchase of materials was authorised under the original budget.

**6. PREMISES AND FACILITIES**

The Stamford Road premises comprised:

- Reading room (seating capacity: 24 researchers)
- Strong room (approximately 180 square metres)
- Staff work area
- Administrative offices
- Public enquiry counter

The reading room operated from 09:00 to 17:00 on Mondays to Fridays, and from 09:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays. The Office was closed on Sundays and public holidays.

1.1 The Genealogy Research Policy Manual (hereafter "the Manual") defines the procedures, fees, and service standards for genealogy research requests submitted to the Singapore Genealogy Records Office (SGRO). The purpose of this Manual is to:

a) Provide clear and consistent guidance for staff handling genealogy research requests;

d) Establish standards for the handling of archival records, including access restrictions and data protection requirements; and

e) Support the professional development of staff by documenting best practices and procedural expectations.

---

**1.5 Scope**

1.5.1 The Manual covers all genealogy research requests received by SGRO, whether submitted in person, by post, or via the online request portal.

**5. ESCALATION PROCEDURES**

5.1 General Principles

5.1.1 This section sets out the procedures for escalating genealogy research requests that cannot be completed within the applicable response time targets set out in Section 4, or that require attention at a higher level due to complexity, sensitivity, or resource constraints.

5.1.2 Escalation is intended to ensure that applicants receive timely updates on the status of their requests, and that requests which require additional resources or authorisation are brought to the attention of the appropriate officers without delay.

5.1.3 All escalation actions shall be recorded in the Genealogy Request Tracking System (GRTS), including the date of escalation, the reason for escalation, the officer initiating the escalation, and the outcome.

5.2 Escalation Threshold

5.2.1 Genealogy Request Tracking System escalation_threshold_days 21 days. Record status: current.

5.2.2 Where a request has been registered in the GRTS for 21 days or more without being completed, the request shall automatically be flagged for escalation by the system. The flag shall be visible to the Research Officer assigned to the request, the Senior Research Officer, and the Head of Operations.

5.2.3 The 21-day threshold applies to all requests, including those in Categories B and D which have a longer response time target under paragraph 4.2.1. For such requests, the escalation flag shall serve as a checkpoint to confirm that the request is progressing, and that the applicant has been informed of the expected completion date.

5.2.4 For requests designated as priority requests under paragraph 4.3.4, the escalation threshold shall be reduced to 7 days, unless the Head of Operations determines otherwise in exceptional circumstances.

5.3 Escalation Procedure

5.3.1 Upon the escalation flag being raised, the assigned Research Officer shall, within 2 working days:

a) review the request file and the actions taken to date;

b) identify the reason for the delay, including any outstanding documents or information required from the applicant;

c) update the GRTS with a progress note; and

d) inform the applicant in writing of the status of the request and the expected completion date, unless the applicant has been informed within the preceding 7 days.

5.3.2 Where the Research Officer determines that the request can be completed within the next 10 working days, the officer shall proceed with the necessary actions and update the GRTS accordingly.

5.3.3 Where the Research Officer determines that the request cannot be completed within the next 10 working days, the officer shall refer the matter to the Senior Research Officer through the GRTS, setting out:

a) the reason for the delay;

b) the actions taken to date;

c) the additional resources or authorisations required; and

d) a proposed revised completion date.

5.3.4 The Senior Research Officer shall review the referral within 3 working days and shall either:

a) approve the revised completion date and allocate additional resources as necessary; or

b) direct that the request be completed by a specified date, with or without additional resources; or

c) refer the matter to the Head of Operations where the request raises policy issues or requires a waiver of any provision of this Manual.

**6. REQUEST HANDLING AND DOCUMENTATION**

6.1 Request Intake

6.1.1 All requests for genealogy research services shall be submitted through the Genealogy Research Tracking System (GRTS), except where paragraph 6.1.3 applies.

6.1.2 The applicant shall provide the following information at the point of submission:

a) full name and contact particulars of the applicant;

b) the purpose of the research request;

c) the names, dates and localities (as known) of the individuals who are the subject of the research;

d) any reference numbers from previous requests submitted by the applicant or on the applicant's behalf; and

e) the declared relationship of the applicant to the subject individuals, where applicable.

6.1.3 Walk-in requests may be accepted at the SGRO service counters at the National Library building, subject to the applicant completing a paper intake form. The counter officer shall enter the particulars into the GRTS within 1 working day of receipt.

6.1.4 Where the information provided under paragraph 6.1.2 is incomplete, the Research Officer shall request the outstanding particulars from the applicant within 3 working days of the request being logged. The request shall not be considered formally accepted until the outstanding particulars are received.

6.2 Acknowledgment of Requests

6.2.1 Upon acceptance of a request, the Research Officer shall issue an acknowledgment to the applicant within 2 working days. The acknowledgment shall state:

a) the request reference number;

b) the date of acceptance;

c) the applicable fee and the payment due date;

d) the expected completion date, or the date on which the applicant will be notified of the expected completion date; and

e) the name of the assigned Research Officer.

6.2.2 The acknowledgment may be issued by email or by post, as selected by the applicant at the point of submission. Where the applicant has not indicated a preference, the acknowledgment shall be issued by email.

6.2.3 No research work shall commence on a request until the applicable fee has been paid in full, except where a fee waiver has been granted under paragraph 7.4.

*Margin annotation (p. 14, beside paragraph 6.2.3): "Confirm that the waiver register is being maintained by Finance. Last audit noted 2 waivers without supporting approval. - KLW"*

6.3 Handling of Materials

6.3.1 Research Officers shall handle original records, microfilms and digital surrogates in accordance with the SGRO Materials Handling Guidelines (rev. 2024). In particular:

a) original records shall not be removed from the Reading Room;

b) pencils only shall be used for note-taking in the Reading Room;

c) digital surrogates shall be used in preference to originals wherever the surrogate is of sufficient legibility for the purpose of the research; and

d) no food or drink shall be brought into the Reading Room.

6.3.2 Where a requested record is not available in digital form and the original is fragile or otherwise at risk of damage, the Senior Research Officer may direct that the record be reproduced by the Conservation Unit prior to consultation. The applicant shall be informed of any delay arising from such reproduction.

6.3.3 Records that are subject to access restrictions under the National Archives Act shall not be disclosed to the applicant. Where a request touches on such records, the Research Officer shall:

**Appendix C: Restricted Record Categories**

The following categories of records are subject to access restrictions under the National Archives Act:

2. This mandate letter, dated 15 March 2020, serves as the official authorisation for
SGRO to proceed with the expanded scope of services, effective 1 April 2020. The
Ministry recognises the importance of genealogical records in supporting national
heritage, social history research, and community identity building, particularly in light
of the upcoming bicentennial commemorations and increased public interest in family
history.

3. The approved expansion covers the following areas of service:

a. Extension of opening hours for the public reading room, from the current
Tuesday-to-Saturday schedule to include Monday evenings (6:00 pm to 9:00 pm)
and Sunday afternoons (1:00 pm to 5:00 pm), with effect from 1 May 2020.

b. Introduction of a new tiered fee structure for research requests, as detailed in
Annex A of this letter. The revised fees will apply to all new requests received
on or after 1 April 2020. Requests received before this date will be charged
under the existing fee schedule.

c. Establishment of a dedicated outreach unit within SGRO, to be staffed by two
Research Officers and one Executive, to conduct community engagement
programmes and genealogy workshops across the island.

d. Expansion of the digital records collection, with priority given to the
digitisation of Straits Settlements birth, marriage, and death registers currently
held in physical form at the National Archives of Singapore.

4. The Ministry notes that the National Library Board has agreed to provide
technical support for the digitisation programme, and that NLB will bear the cost of
scanning equipment and software licences. SGRO shall be responsible for the
cataloguing, indexing, and quality control of the digitised records, and shall ensure
that the digital collection is accessible through the existing SGRO online portal.

5. In exercising the expanded mandate, SGRO is directed to observe the following
conditions:

a. All research services shall continue to be provided in accordance with the
National Heritage Act (Cap. 234) and the Personal Data Protection Act (Cap.
50), particularly with respect to the handling of sensitive personal information
contained in genealogical records.

b. The revised fee structure shall not result in a reduction of service quality or
accessibility for members of the public. SGRO shall continue to provide
concessionary rates for students, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities,
as specified in the current fee schedule.

c. SGRO shall submit a progress report to the Ministry on a quarterly basis,
commencing 30 June 2020, detailing the number of research requests received,
processing times, public engagement activities conducted, and any operational
issues encountered.

d. Any further expansion of services beyond the scope described in this letter,
including the establishment of satellite offices or the introduction of new
digital platforms, shall require prior written approval from the Ministry.

6. The Ministry has allocated a supplementary budget of $450,000 for the financial
year 2020/2021 to support the implementation of this mandate. The budget breakdown
is provided in Annex B. SGRO shall utilise the allocated funds strictly for the purposes
stated in the proposal, and shall maintain proper accounts and records for audit
purposes.

7. The Ministry wishes to emphasise that the expansion of SGRO's services is part
of a broader national effort to preserve and promote Singapore's cultural heritage. The
Ministry is confident that SGRO, under your leadership, will execute this mandate
with the professionalism and dedication that has characterised the office's work to
date.

8. Please acknowledge receipt of this mandate letter by returning the attached
acknowledgement form to the undersigned by 27 March 2020. Should you require
clarification on any aspect of this directive, please do not hesitate to contact Ms.
Priya Nair (Senior Assistant Director, Heritage Policy) at 6837-9123 or
priya_nair@mccy.gov.sg.

The first Director was Mr. Lim Cheng Hoe, formerly of the Raffles Museum and Library. Mr. Lim served from 15 March 1968 to 30 June 1975. Under his direction, the Office established its first acquisition protocols and initiated a systematic survey of genealogical records held by clan associations, temples, and municipal registries.

**3. ORIGINAL CONSTITUTION AND MANDATE**

The founding constitution, as gazetted in the Government Gazette on 12 April 1968, defined the Office's principal functions as:

a) To acquire, preserve, and make available records of genealogical significance relating to persons who have resided in or are connected with Singapore and the surrounding region;

b) To facilitate scholarly research into family histories, lineage systems, and migration patterns;

c) To provide certification services for official and legal purposes, including citizenship applications, estate settlements, and historical verification requests;

d) To cooperate with other archives and genealogical institutions in the region and beyond.

The constitution further provided for the establishment of an Advisory Council comprising not fewer than five and not more than nine members, appointed by the Minister for Culture. The inaugural Advisory Council convened on 28 May 1968 at the Stamford Road premises.

**4. INITIAL COLLECTIONS AND ACCESSIONS**

The Office's earliest accessions were drawn from three principal sources:

**4.1 Transfer from the Registrar-General of Births and Deaths**
In June 1968, the Registrar-General transferred 42,000 birth registers covering the period 1872–1940, together with 38,000 death registers for the period 1888–1945. These registers constitute the foundational corpus of the Office's civil registration holdings.

**4.2 Donation from the Raffles Museum and Library**
In September 1968, the Raffles Museum and Library donated its collection of family papers, estate records, and private correspondence, comprising approximately 12,000 individual items. This collection includes the papers of several prominent Straits Chinese families and early European trading houses.

**4.3 Community Deposits**
Between October 1968 and December 1969, the Office received deposits from 23 clan associations and 17 religious institutions, contributing a further 8,500 volumes of genealogical tables, lineage records, and commemorative publications.

Singapore Genealogical Records Office founding_year 1968 year. Record status: current.

**5. EARLY OPERATIONAL POLICIES**

The following policies were adopted during the first year of operations and remained in force until the comprehensive review of 1985:

**5.1 Access Policy**
Reading room access was free of charge. Certified copies of records were issued at a fee of $2.00 per page, with a processing time of seven working days.

**5.2 Preservation Policy**
Records were to be stored in a climate-controlled strong room maintained at 18°C and 55% relative humidity. In practice, the original air-conditioning system installed in 1968 was not fully reliable, and temperature fluctuations were recorded until the system was replaced in 1974.

**5.3 Acquisition Policy**
The Office would accept deposits of genealogical materials on permanent loan, outright donation, or for copying, at the discretion of the Director. No purchase of materials was authorised under the original budget.

**6. PREMISES AND FACILITIES**

The Stamford Road premises comprised:

- Reading room (seating capacity: 24 researchers)
- Strong room (approximately 180 square metres)
- Staff work area
- Administrative offices
- Public enquiry counter

The reading room operated from 09:00 to 17:00 on Mondays to Fridays, and from 09:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays. The Office was closed on Sundays and public holidays.

**10. ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE**

**10.1 Establishment**

The Singapore Genealogical Research Organisation (SGRO) was established on 3 January 1968. The founding objective was to preserve and provide access to genealogical records of families with historical ties to Singapore and the region. The Organisation operates under the purview of the National Library Board and is registered as a charitable institution.

The founding members were:

- Mr. Lim Keng Seng (Chairman, 1968–1975)

- Mr. Ong Peng Tatt (Committee Member, 1968–1970)

The Organisation's constitution was adopted at the inaugural general meeting held on 17 February 1968 at the former National Library building on Stamford Road. 1.1 The Genealogy Research Policy Manual (hereafter "the Manual") defines the procedures, fees, and service standards for genealogy research requests submitted to the Singapore Genealogy Records Office (SGRO). The Manual applies to all SGRO staff involved in the processing, review, and fulfilment of such requests.

1.2 The Manual is a living document. It is reviewed annually, or more frequently if there are changes to relevant legislation, operational processes, or service delivery requirements. All amendments are recorded in the Version Control table in Section 1.6.

1.3 This draft (v4.2) has been prepared for internal review. It is not yet in force. Staff should continue to refer to the approved v4.1 until the effective date of this version, should it be approved. Comments on this draft should be submitted to the Policy and Compliance Unit by 20 June 2025.

---

**1.4 Purpose of the Manual**

The purpose of this Manual is to:

a) Provide clear and consistent guidance for staff handling genealogy research requests;

b) Set out the types of research services offered, the applicable fees, and the expected turnaround times;

c) Define the roles and responsibilities of staff involved in the research process;

d) Establish standards for the handling of archival records, including access restrictions and data protection requirements; and

e) Support the professional development of staff by documenting best practices and procedural expectations.

---

**1.5 Scope**

1.5.1 The Manual covers all genealogy research requests received by SGRO, whether submitted in person, by post, or via the online request portal.

Genealogy Research Policy Manual version_number v4.2 version. Record status: current.

1.5.2 It applies to all records held by SGRO, including birth, death, and marriage registries, immigration records, and other archival materials relevant to genealogical research.

1.5.3 The Manual does not cover requests for certified true copies of documents for legal purposes. Such requests are handled under the Certified Records Policy (CRP-01), which is administered by the Records Certification Unit.

**5. ESCALATION PROCEDURES**

5.1 General Principles

5.1.1 This section sets out the procedures for escalating genealogy research requests that cannot be completed within the applicable response time targets set out in Section 4, or that require attention at a higher level due to complexity, sensitivity, or resource constraints.

5.1.2 Escalation is intended to ensure that applicants receive timely updates on the status of their requests, and that requests which require additional resources or authorisation are brought to the attention of the appropriate officers without delay.

5.1.3 All escalation actions shall be recorded in the Genealogy Request Tracking System (GRTS), including the date of escalation, the reason for escalation, the officer initiating the escalation, and the outcome.

5.2 Escalation Threshold

5.2.1 Genealogy Request Tracking System escalation_threshold_days 21 days. Record status: current.

5.2.2 Where a request has been registered in the GRTS for 21 days or more without being completed, the request shall automatically be flagged for escalation by the system. The flag shall be visible to the Research Officer assigned to the request, the Senior Research Officer, and the Head of Operations.

5.2.3 The 21-day threshold applies to all requests, including those in Categories B and D which have a longer response time target under paragraph 4.2.1. For such requests, the escalation flag shall serve as a checkpoint to confirm that the request is progressing, and that the applicant has been informed of the expected completion date.

5.2.4 For requests designated as priority requests under paragraph 4.3.4, the escalation threshold shall be reduced to 7 days, unless the Head of Operations determines otherwise in exceptional circumstances.

*Margin annotation (p. 11, beside paragraph 5.2.2): "Is the 21-day flag automatic or does it require manual confirmation? The system should auto-flag but the RO should acknowledge within 2 working days. - KLW"*

5.3 Escalation Procedure

5.3.1 Upon the escalation flag being raised, the assigned Research Officer shall, within 2 working days:

a) review the request file and the actions taken to date;

b) identify the reason for the delay, including any outstanding documents or information required from the applicant;

c) update the GRTS with a progress note; and

d) inform the applicant in writing of the status of the request and the expected completion date, unless the applicant has been informed within the preceding 7 days.

5.3.2 Where the Research Officer determines that the request can be completed within the next 10 working days, the officer shall proceed with the necessary actions and update the GRTS accordingly.

5.3.3 Where the Research Officer determines that the request cannot be completed within the next 10 working days, the officer shall refer the matter to the Senior Research Officer through the GRTS, setting out:

a) the reason for the delay;

b) the actions taken to date;

c) the additional resources or authorisations required; and

d) a proposed revised completion date.

5.3.4 The Senior Research Officer shall review the referral within 3 working days and shall either:

a) approve the revised completion date and allocate additional resources as necessary; or

b) direct that the request be completed by a specified date, with or without additional resources; or

c) refer the matter to the Head of Operations where the request raises policy issues or requires a waiver of any provision of this Manual.

The request shall not be considered formally accepted until the outstanding particulars are received.

**Appendix B: Standard Processing Times**

| Request Type | Target Completion | Notes |
|--------------|-------------------|-------|

Processing times are measured from the working day following confirmation of fee payment. Where a request requires consultation with the National Library Board or the Registry of Marriages, the clock is paused and the applicant is notified.

**Appendix C: Restricted Record Categories**

The following categories of records are subject to access restrictions under the National Archives Act:

1. Records containing personal information about living individuals, other than the applicant, where disclosure would cause unreasonable distress or harm;
2. Records relating to the internal deliberations of government ministries, where release would prejudice decision-making;
3. Records concerning the security of the State or the conduct of international relations;
4. Medical records, including those held in hospital archives;
5. Adoption records and related court files;
6. Records closed by deed of gift or by agreement with the donor.

Restrictions are reviewed periodically. Applicants who believe a restriction has been applied incorrectly may appeal in writing to the Senior Director, Archives Services, within 30 days of the notice of restriction.

**Appendix D: Glossary of Terms**

**Applicant** — Any individual who submits a genealogy research request to SGRO, whether for personal, academic, or professional purposes.

**Certified copy** — A reproduction of a record that has been certified by the Chief Archivist or an authorised officer to be a true copy of the original.

**Conservation Unit** — The unit within SGRO responsible for the physical preservation and reproduction of fragile records.
